title: Study and teaching at home
word: a teaching role in the house
hookLine: three teachers, three answers, and an Upanishad that won't vote
carry: svadhyaya and pravachana: study, and pass it on
tomorrow: who teaches when the teacher's away?

cards: Ask three relatives what a kid most needs to learn and you'll have three answers before dessert. Be honest. Be disciplined.
Know where you come from. The Taittiriya Upanishad has its own version of that dinner table. Three named teachers, three different answers.
And the text does something unusual with them.

teach.b: First, the setting. The Taittiriya walks through a household, item by item. Right order, and learning and teaching.
Truth, and learning and teaching. Self-control, calm, the household fires, guests, children, grandchildren, and after every one the same pair comes back: svadhyaya and pravachana, study and teaching.
It sets them beside the guest at the door and the grandchild in the next room. Then the three voices.
Satyavachas Rathitara says: truth. His case: without honesty, everything else in the house is built on sand.

Taponitya Paurushishti says: tapas, austerity, discipline. His case: nothing learned holds without the steady effort that holds it. And Naka Maudgalya says: learning and teaching alone, for that is tapas, that is tapas.
His case: study and passing it on aren't a break from discipline. They are the discipline. Notice that Naka doesn't throw out austerity.
He folds it into the reading and the teaching. And the Upanishad itself keeps all three names on the page. It doesn't declare a winner.
So here is the Hindu teaching, plainly: svadhyaya, your own study of the sacred word, and pravachana, handing it on, are a duty of the household, not only of the school.
A teaching role in the house belongs to whoever keeps the pair going, next to everything else.

how: In some Hindu homes elders tell stories, teach prayers and keep a little daily reading going; the Taittiriya's list (1.9) is sometimes quoted to say study and teaching belong at home, not only at school.

games.q: what does “a teaching role in the house” mean?
o: the eldest son's right to run the family rites
a paid job teaching children in a temple school
passing on what you know, inside everyday home life

games.q: three teachers, three answers. tap the pairs.

s: Naka Maudgalya rejects austerity in favor of study
he says study and teaching are themselves tapas: that is tapas, that is tapas.
the Taittiriya names three teachers and doesn't declare a winner
all three names and answers stay on the page.
the list puts study and teaching apart from home life, for school
they come after every item: the fires, guests, children, grandchildren.

games.q: your family argues: honesty first, discipline first, or study first. you lean toward study. state the best case for discipline, in Taponitya's spirit.
o: nothing learned holds without steady effort to hold it.
study is a waste of time without punishment.
discipline matters only for monks, not homes.
games.why: Taponitya names tapas, the steady effort. and Naka answers by folding it in: study and teaching are that effort. the text keeps both.

practice: Pick one short line you keep: a verse of the Gita, a prayer, a line from this week. Read it aloud once, slowly: that's svadhyaya. Then say what it means in your own words, as if to a child: that's pravachana.
If someone's home tonight, tell it to them.

wordCard.voice: A teaching role in the house: study and teaching set beside every part of home life, as the Taittiriya lists them, with three teachers left standing side by side.

orig.note: Sanskrit: study, one's own recitation; in Taittiriya 1.9 it's paired every time with pravachana, teaching.

carryVoice: Your line: svadhyaya and pravachana, study, and pass it on. In the Taittiriya, three teachers keep their seats at the table. That's today, done.

sources.ref: Taittiriya Upanishad 1.9 (right order, truth, austerity, self-control, calm, the fires, the fire offering, guests, the human, offspring, begetting, grandchildren, each with learning and teaching; Satyavachas Rathitara says truth, Taponitya Paurushishti austerity, Naka Maudgalya learning and teaching alone, for that is austerity, that is austerity)
